title: Left View of a Binary Tree
statement:
Imagine standing to the left of a binary tree and looking at it horizontally. At every level, the only node you can see is the **leftmost node of that level**: the first node you meet when you read that level from left to right. A node counts as being on a level by its depth, regardless of whether it is a left or a right child (a level's leftmost node may be a right child when nodes to its left are missing).

Print the values of the visible nodes, from the root level down to the deepest level.
inputFormat: A single line with the level-order serialization of the tree: the values of the nodes read level by level, left to right, with `null` marking a missing child. Children of a `null` entry are not listed, and trailing `null` entries are omitted. The first token is always the root (never `null`).
outputFormat: Print the values of the left view from top to bottom on one line, separated by single spaces.
constraints: The tree has at most 5000 levels, so recursive solutions fit in the call stack

examples.explanation: Level 0 is [1], level 1 is [2, 3], level 2 is [4, 5, 6] and level 3 is [7, 8]. The first value of each level is 1, 2, 4 and 7.
The root 5 has only a right child 8. Level 1 is [8] and level 2 is [6, 9], so the view is 5, 8, 6 even though 5 and 8 have no left children.
A single node is visible by itself.

hints: You need one value per level, so think about a traversal that visits the nodes of a level together.
Run a breadth-first search and record the first node dequeued at each level.
A depth-first search works too: visit the left child before the right child and save a node's value only the first time its depth is reached.

import sys
from collections import deque
from typing import List, Optional


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


def build_tree(tokens: List[str]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
    if not tokens or tokens[0] == 'null':
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(tokens[0]))
    queue = deque([root])
    i = 1
    while queue and i < len(tokens):
        node = queue.popleft()
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] != 'null':
            node.left = TreeNode(int(tokens[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] != 'null':
            node.right = TreeNode(int(tokens[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root
